title: crosslang-session-unifier-compact-retries-and-stream-ergonomics
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce cross-language SessionMiddleware + compact RetryPolicy; bump python/sdk -> v2.4.0, typescript/sdk -> v1.7.0, go/sdk -> v1.5.3; ergonomics improvements for streaming iterators and credential warm-up. No breaking API changes for public surface; opt-in config flags for advanced behaviors.
description:
Motivation: teams building long-lived streaming flows need consistent session semantics, predictable credential handoff, and compact retry profiles across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. This PR consolidates previous ad-hoc session shims into a small cross-language SessionMiddleware plus a compact RetryPolicy abstraction that encodes per-stream backoff hints and warmup directives. The goal is pragmatic parity: single conceptual model for session lifecycle + minimal ergonomic primitives for users to adopt without rewriting existing streaming code.

Summary of changes: added a new SessionMiddleware interface and reference implementations in python/ts/go; introduced RetryPolicy compact profile and three defaults (fast, balanced, patient); replaced legacy StreamCursor+Resumer plumbing with a simplified PullStreamCursor that exposes a single async iterator/chan-friendly API per language; added a compact credential-swap adapter that performs background token refresh and exposes a lightweight event hook for telemetry; bumped SDK package versions (py 2.4.0, ts 1.7.0, go 1.5.3); updated docs and migration guide.

Notable files and diffs (high level): see files_changed for concrete list. Changes are intentionally small per-language: python focuses on async iterator ergonomics, typescript adds an ergonomic pullstream facade and a Promise-based warmup API, go focuses on channel-friendly PullStreamCursor and low-allocation retry loop. No changes to server APIs or wire protocol.

Compatibility & migration notes: default behavior is backward compatible. New functionality is behind opt-in flags: SessionMiddleware is not injected by default; SDKs provide a one-line opt-in helper (e.g. RedwoodSession.enable_default_middleware()). Applications that previously depended on internal cursor rehydration should follow the migration guide included in docs/migration/session-unifier.md.

Testing and validation: unit tests and integration matrix added for each SDK; added cross-language integration test that exercises a long-lived streaming scenario, credential rotation, and failover to fallback model. Performance bench: small improvement in median tail-latency under high concurrent stream counts due to reduced allocation churn and simplified cursor state.

Rollout plan: merged to main behind feature-flag in platform; gradual rollout to hosted and dedicated customers using canary groups. Follow-ups: telemetry enrichment for per-stream retry buckets (ENG-2104), a docs RFC to align examples across languages (ENG-2112), and a future opt-in server hook to surface session state for observability (ENG-2176).
